references.text: This verse refers to Jesus and the disciples descending from the mountain after the transfiguration, where Jesus instructs them not to tell anyone what they have seen until the Son of Man has risen from the dead, which relates to the disciples' wonder in Mark 9:10.
In this passage, the Sadducees challenge Jesus with a question about the resurrection, which is relevant to the disciples' discussion in Mark 9:10.
Similar to Matthew 22:23-33, here the Sadducees challenge Jesus regarding the resurrection, providing background for the disciples' wonder in Mark 9:10.

The Acts of the Apostles describes how Peter and John were arrested for teaching the people and proclaiming the resurrection of Jesus from the dead, which provides context to the disciples' question in Mark 9:10.
Paul's preaching in Athens about Jesus and the resurrection sparks curiosity among the philosophers, reflecting the early Christian church's focus on the resurrection, related to Mark 9:10.
Paul uses his belief in the resurrection as a defense before the Sanhedrin, underscoring the importance of faith in the resurrection, which the disciples also wondered about in Mark 9:10.

Paul's defense of his faith includes an affirmation of hope in the resurrection for both the righteous and the unrighteous, offering insight into the early Christian understanding of the resurrection discussed in Mark 9:10.
Paul's extensive teaching on the resurrection in 1 Corinthians provides theological background to the disciples' question in Mark 9:10.
